findings.description: Sixteen setups (adversarial-review.bats, adversarial-review-e2e.bats, bug-809-status-note.bats, cycle-109-*.bats, cycle-124-dispatch-budgets.bats, cycle-baseline-capture.bats, ledger-isolation-discovery.bats, model-adapter-probe-integration.bats, spiral-harness-adversarial-dissent.bats, wire-schemas-api-safe.bats, input-size-consumers.bats, butterfreezone-gen-sha256-portability.bats, adversarial-review-degraded-on-rejection.bats, adversarial-review-kf-011-debug.bats, adversarial-review-hallucination-filter.bats) export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR" with the comment 'the CLI lock is this test's own, never the per-user one a live dissent holds (run 23)'. The reviewer context for the thirty-eighth run (round 1am, CMP-255) records that the dissent script's locks 'move to a private ~/.cache/loa/headless-locks-<uid>'. If that move made ~/.cache the primary lock base rather than a fallback below $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR, every one of these exports is a no-op for lock isolation and the comment is stale: the suites would again resolve the operator's per-user lock directory, which is exactly the queue-behind-a-live-claude.lock failure the run-16/run-23 notes describe (NRM-26). The diff cannot show which reading is right because adversarial-review.sh is not in it.
findings.failure_mode: A suite that reaches a *-headless hop (or whose stubbed hop still takes the per-binary flock) waits up to the lock-wait cap behind a live dissent's claude.lock, or holds that lock and delays the live run; the comment misleads the next reader into assuming isolation that is not there.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm how adversarial-review.sh resolves the CLI lock directory after CMP-255. If $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is still the first candidate, leave the exports and shorten the comment to cite the resolution order. If ~/.cache/loa/headless-locks-<uid> is now primary, isolate through the script's lock-directory knob (or a per-test HOME) in a shared helper instead of sixteen copies of the export, and have the e3 lint check that knob rather than XDG_RUNTIME_DIR.

findings.description: The e3 lint's patterns have gaps that let the fallback it forbids back in, and one over-match. (1) _e3_xdg_fallback uses 'XDG_RUNTIME_DIR[=][^;]*mktemp': the assign-default form ': "${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:=$(mktemp -d)}"' has ':' before '=' and does not match, yet it creates exactly the unswept per-test mktemp directory the lint exists to refuse. (2) _e3_tmpdir_fallback ('[{]BATS_TEST_TMPDIR[:]?[-]') and the case-branch grep ('BATS_TEST_TMPDIR[:]?[-][^}]*mktemp') miss '${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:=$(mktemp -d)}' for the same reason, and that spelling also satisfies none of _e3_guarded's alternatives, so a suite written that way passes both the guard check and the fallback check while behaving like the old ':-' fallback. (3) '[^;]*' stops only at ';', not at '&&', '||' or '|', so 'export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR" && T="$(mktemp -d)"' is reported as a fallback although the mktemp belongs to another statement, the case the thirty-third-run fix (DISS-C-003) meant to exclude. None of the fixture legs in the test exercise ':=' or an '&&'-joined statement, so the gaps are not pinned.
findings.failure_mode: A future setup that defaults XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or BATS_TEST_TMPDIR with ':=' and mktemp passes the lint and leaves an unswept temp directory per test; conversely a legitimate '&&'-joined setup line fails adversarial-review.bats with a false 'falls back to an unswept mktemp XDG_RUNTIME_DIR'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use 'XDG_RUNTIME_DIR[:]?[=][^;&|]*mktemp' in _e3_xdg_fallback, '[{]BATS_TEST_TMPDIR[:]?[-=]' in _e3_tmpdir_fallback and 'BATS_TEST_TMPDIR[:]?[-=][^}]*mktemp' in the case branch, and add fixture legs for ': "${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:=$(mktemp -d)}"' (must trip) and 'export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR" && T="$(mktemp -d)"' (must not trip), each with the '%s' splice so the lines never match themselves.

findings.description: The new pre-source check _jq_pair_extracted_whole validates only the second extraction (the '/^_adv_jq_pair() {/,/^}/' range). The first extraction, ext.sh from the banner range '/# Dissenter Hallucination Filter/,/# Finding ID Computation/', is still concatenated into filter-fns.sh and sourced unchecked. If either banner is renamed, the sed range runs to end-of-file or yields nothing, and the failure surfaces as the same opaque 'unexpected end of file' or 'command not found' from source that e3 DISS-C-003 was raised against; the self-lint test added in this hunk ('setup checks the _adv_jq_pair extraction before it sources it') pins ordering only for the jq-pair extraction. Separately, the next-line heuristic in _jq_pair_extracted_whole treats any indented non-blank line after the closing brace as body, so an indented comment such as '  # next helper' following the function in adversarial-review.sh would fail every test's setup with 'extraction ended inside its body' although the extraction is whole and bash -n would have passed it.
findings.failure_mode: A banner rename or a cut inside the hallucination-filter block fails all 20 tests in setup with an uninformative shell parse error; an indented comment line after _adv_jq_pair's closing brace fails all tests in setup with a false 'ended inside its body'.
findings.suggested_fix: Before 'source filter-fns.sh', run 'bash -n filter-fns.sh' and name the file on failure, and assert ext.sh is non-empty and contains both banners (grep -c for each, expecting 1). In _jq_pair_extracted_whole, let a next line matching '^[[:space:]]*#' count as not-body (or drop the heuristic and rely on bash -n alone, since any column-0 '}' that is not the function's own leaves its '{' open and fails bash -n).
